correctness.rationale: Every input decomposes into positive weighted binary level sets, reducing the exact quotient norm to cuts. Exact column formula and monotone ordering reduce general cuts to a harmonic inequality F(n,k)>0. Its positive n-increment applies for n>=2k; the k=2,3,4 anchors at n=9, the seventeen k=5..21 exact values at n=2k, and the all-k>=22 logarithmic lower bound cover every larger n. Independent exhaustive exact-rational enumeration verifies all 494 proper cuts in n=2..8. e_1 attains the closed formula. The threshold and logarithmic asymptotic follow from harmonic identities; finite experiments alone are not used to infer the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The unweighted Gini seminorm is a canonical sample-dispersion functional and complete-graph total variation. The theorem solves its natural exact Cesàro stability invariant for all dimensions, gives an attaining spike, identifies the sharp phase change from contraction to amplification at six coordinates, and proves log n growth. The difference from strict contraction (1-1/n) in finite adjacent-edge variation is a structural nonlocal-geometry distinction; the result is not a mere arbitrary finite lookup.
